subsystems.name: Physical qubit layer
subsystems.role: the raw quantum elements — superconducting circuits, trapped ions or neutral atoms — that store and process quantum states and inevitably make errors.

subsystems.name: Encoding layer
subsystems.role: spreads one logical qubit's information across many physical qubits using an error-correcting code.

subsystems.name: Syndrome extraction
subsystems.role: repeatedly measures parity checks between neighbours without collapsing the encoded information.

subsystems.name: Classical decoder
subsystems.role: reads the stream of syndrome bits and infers the most likely error pattern in real time.

subsystems.name: Fault-tolerant operation layer
subsystems.role: performs logical gates on encoded qubits while keeping errors correctable.
parts: lattice surgery or transversal gate logic

subsystems.name: Cryogenics and infrastructure
subsystems.role: keeps superconducting qubits near absolute zero and shields them from noise.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate physical qubits
buildSteps.detail: Superconducting circuits are patterned on a chip with lithography; trapped-ion or neutral-atom systems load ions or atoms into a trap or array instead.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the machine
buildSteps.detail: Each qubit's frequency, readout and one- and two-qubit gates are tuned until single-qubit and two-qubit error rates are low and stable.

buildSteps.title: Choose the code and layout
buildSteps.detail: Qubits are arranged on a grid matching the code, typically a surface code where each data qubit is checked by four neighbouring ancillas.

buildSteps.title: Initialise and encode
buildSteps.detail: The array is prepared in a known state and the logical qubit is written into it by entangling the physical qubits.

buildSteps.title: Extract syndromes in cycles
buildSteps.detail: Ancilla qubits are entangled with their neighbours, measured, and reset; this repeats every few microseconds to catch errors faster than they accumulate.

buildSteps.title: Decode and correct
buildSteps.detail: The classical decoder turns repeated syndrome patterns into a correction, which is applied as a Pauli frame update rather than a physical pulse, so the logical state stays intact.

buildSteps.title: Grow and benchmark the logical qubit
buildSteps.detail: Larger-distance codes are built (distance 3, then 5, then 7) and measured to confirm that error rates fall as physical qubit count rises.

buildSteps.title: Run logical gates
buildSteps.detail: Logical operations such as lattice surgery merge and split encoded patches, building a fault-tolerant instruction set.

prerequisites.tech: Physical qubit fidelities above the code threshold
prerequisites.why: error correction only suppresses errors if physical error rates sit below a threshold set by the code.
syndromes must be read and ancillas reused many times within the qubit coherence time.
corrections are needed faster than the next syndrome cycle, which forces dedicated hardware.
thousands of wires and control channels must be squeezed into a fridge without adding heat or noise.
Clifford gates alone are not enough; non-Clifford gates need distillation or special code structures.

pathway.milestone: small logical qubits of a few dozen physical qubits showing error suppression as code distance grows (demonstrated on superconducting hardware in 2024)
pathway.unlocks: confidence that scaling the code, not just the chip, reduces logical error.

pathway.milestone: sustained logical qubits with thousands of physical qubits and logical error rates around one in a million
pathway.unlocks: early fault-tolerant demonstrations of small but genuinely useful quantum circuits.

pathway.milestone: tens to hundreds of high-quality logical qubits with full fault-tolerant gate sets
pathway.unlocks: chemistry and materials simulation beyond classical reach.

pathway.milestone: thousands of logical qubits at very low error rates
pathway.unlocks: cryptographically relevant algorithms and large-scale optimisation.
